findings.detail: Replace a tracked submodule checkout with a symlink, leaving the replacement unstaged. The real index still contains the gitlink, so collection includes this path even though the temporary disk index represents a symlink. This check then aborts the entire scope collection. A legitimate gitlink-to-symlink change cannot reach either review workflow. Distinguish a replacement symlink from an initialized checkout and review its link text without traversing it.
findings.evidence: collect_submodules unions gitlinks from the real and temporary indexes at lines 314–318, then unconditionally rejects a symlink at line 322. Collection runs before the diff buckets are gathered. Both canonical review-scope copies contain this code and are byte-identical.
findings.title: Sibling input forms: gitlink-to-symlink replacements abort scope collection

findings.detail: A submodule can have a normal configured name and a checkout path such as -vendor. Git's quoted -C argument accepts that path, but the following cd interprets it as options and fails, rejecting the initialized checkout. The recursive launch repeats that cd, and the uninitialized branch passes the same option-like path to find. Use an absolute child path consistently across these operations.
findings.evidence: Lines 326 and 328 pass the repository-relative path directly to cd; line 335 does so for find. A standalone platform probe, /bin/bash -c 'builtin cd "-review-sample"', returned status 1 with 'cd: -r: invalid option', confirming that quoting does not prevent option parsing. Both canonical collectors share these call sites.
findings.title: Untrusted data in commands: option-like submodule paths reach cd and find
